# Pull Request

## Description

> Please include a summary of the change and which issue is fixed.
> Include relevant motivation and context.

## Related Issue

> Fixes #issue (e.g. "Fixes #1"), or "none" if no relevant issues.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] New physics / community code
- [ ] New analysis or diagnostic
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Other (please explain):

## How has this been tested?

> Describe what you actually ran.
> For physics-relevant changes, what did you compare against
> (analytic result, literature value, or a previous run).

## Checklist

- [ ] My code follows the project's style guidelines (`ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` pass)
- [ ] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [ ] I have commented my code where necessary
- [ ] No new large data files committed (see `.gitignore`)
- [ ] Any new dependency added to `env.yml`
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
